items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: So I got with them and went on the road with them, and I must have stayed with them for three years... went on the road with Charlie Taylor, see, again.

ctx.x: No, I mean after you were in Chicago. Huh? After you were in Chicago. Well. Things started getting slow, you said.

That's what I said, and this fellow come through with them Brown Manigan I told you about, Charlie Taylor. Mm-hmm. Well, he hadn't heard of me a long time, so he come up to a place where, well he used to work with Miramac, and then had Miramac Miramacos when he first started out. So he had his own show, and he come up and asked, what was I doing? I told him nothing, so he asked me how would I like to make a trip with him. Mm-hmm. So I got with them and went on the road with them, and I must have stayed with them…
Well that's the thing most that killed me up. Well now, who did you work with in New York?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: we did Oz with a show by the name of Charlie Taylor... some man hired the band... we played on the boat

ctx.x: Yeah, you said it on the other day. But any other, any other things besides that, your job or things? No. I just wondered, since they put you in that.

Taylor, one thing I can say, we did Oz with a show by the name of Charlie Taylor. We got in some town up in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and we was off, and some man hired the band, you know, and we played on the boat all night's after night.
